correctness.rationale: Exact face enumeration gives the stated face vector. The package matching is acyclic and leaves one critical 0-cell, four critical 3-cells, and one critical 4-cell. The four relevant gradient-path counts are \((2,0,2,2)\), so every integral Morse-boundary coefficient has absolute value at most two. Independent boundary computations over both \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_3\) give reduced Betti numbers four in degree three and one in degree four, forcing that integer Morse differential to vanish. The attaching map of the unique 4-cell to \(\bigvee^4S^3\) is then null by the Hurewicz isomorphism. An independent reconstruction reproduced the face vector, critical cells, path counts, and modular homology.

originality.rationale: Biyikoğlu--Civan Example 3.9 already takes the Möbius--Kantor graph \(G(8,3)\) and explicitly says that it first determines the homotopy type of its independence complex. The same example records \(\operatorname{Ind}(G-x)\simeq\bigvee^3S^3\) and \(\operatorname{Ind}(G-N[x])\simeq S^2\vee S^3\); applying the decomposition theorem invoked in that example yields \(\bigvee^4S^3\vee S^4\). Thus the audited finite Morse certificate is an independent proof of a previously determined exact homotopy type, not a new scientific result.
